messages:
olivia: Quick QA — after flipping `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-proxy-protocol: "*"` on inference-gateway NLB, some k8s readiness probes started failing. Healthchecks show TLS handshake errors. Anyone seen this when switching to proxy-protocol + TLS passthrough?

sam: Did we change targetType? nodeport vs ip? NLB + proxy protocol often expects instance targets or apps that understand the PROXY header.

olivia: Here is the svc we patched in staging:```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-proxy-protocol: "*"
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  ports:
  - port: 443
    targetPort: 1443
  externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster
```

raj: externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster will NAT traffic through kube-proxy so the pod sees different SRC IPs. Also important: when proxy-protocol is enabled the target (pod/process) must parse the PROXY headers before the TLS handshake. If it doesn't, TLS handshake fails.

olivia: Ah — that matches the error logs: `tls: first record does not look like a TLS handshake`. So our pods are getting the PROXY v2 bytes and choking. Two options I see: disable proxy-protocol, or run a proxy (envoy/nginx) that understands PROXY v2 in front of the app.

jen: Another angle: change the targetGroup attributes in TF. We can set `proxy_protocol_v2 = false` for the TG that backs the NLB (so AWS strips nothing) OR move to targetType = ip + instance mode depending on how we want source IP surfaced. Also consider health check type: if NLB is TCP passthrough, use TCP health checks rather than HTTP GET.

sam: Quick checklist: 1) If we want to keep proxy-protocol on, add sidecar that accepts v2 and forwards plain TLS to app. 2) If we want app to see client IP, set externalTrafficPolicy: Local + nodePort mapping + NLB TCP health to nodePort. 3) For ALB (L7) we can get X-Forwarded-For and keep HTTP healthchecks.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: infra/tf plan created for change P-4421 — toggling `proxy_protocol_v2` on target group is possible in TF. Will not apply without approval.

olivia: Plan for now: revert the `aws-load-balancer-proxy-protocol` annotation in staging to restore previous behavior, then do a canary where we: (A) deploy envoy sidecar that accepts PROXY v2, (B) use targetType=ip in a TF branch and validate healthchecks, (C) if green, roll to prod with a controlled TTL. I'll open a PR and RFC. ping @sam for review.

sam: :thumbsup: Prefer envoy canary first. Also add a note to the infra README about requirements for apps behind NLB with proxy-protocol.

jen: Minor gotcha — our readinessProbe is `HTTP GET /live` on :8080. If we switch NLB healthchecks to TCP, those checks won't validate the app liveness endpoint. Keep k8s probes as-is; ensure nodeport healthchecks target the nodeport that kube-proxy forwards to pod.

olivia: Good call. I'll add that to the PR checklist. Thanks all — I'll follow up with links to the PR and the TF plan. Leaving the thread open for any other gotchas or if someone wants a different approach.
